prompt:
Repair the flights package's asyncio single-flight coalescer. Public API: from flights import Coalescer; construct Coalescer() inside or outside a running loop, then await coalescer.run(key, factory). run is an async method. One instance is used on one event loop only; keys may be any hashable object (including None). Unhashable keys raise TypeError. No thread safety or cross-loop support is required.

A factory is a zero-argument callable returning an awaitable. For overlapping calls with equal keys, invoke only the first caller's factory, exactly once, in one shared asyncio Task. Ignore other callers' factories entirely. Different keys must run independently. Every successful waiter receives the identical result object, including None. pending_count is a read-only property counting unfinished shared tasks, not waiters; it starts at zero and does not include completed tasks.

Cancellation belongs to each waiter: cancelling any waiter raises asyncio.CancelledError in that waiter without cancelling the shared task or any other waiter. This applies even if the initiating waiter or every waiter is cancelled. Work with no remaining waiters must continue. A later caller joining before that work finishes must share it, not start another factory. If the factory fails, every noncancelled waiter receives that failure, and a later call can retry. Support factories that raise synchronously when invoked as well as awaitables that raise. If the factory's awaitable cancels itself, all its current waiters receive CancelledError and a subsequent call may retry.

This is coalescing, not caching: evict a shared task on either success, failure, or factory cancellation. A call after completion must start new work, even if an older waiter's cleanup has not run yet. Stale completion cleanup must not discard newer work for the same key. A task failure with no remaining waiters must be retrieved so the loop does not report "Task exception was never retrieved". Preserve exception objects (do not wrap failures). The provided FlightBook and Coalescer currently split task ownership incorrectly; fix their interaction, not only the common success path. Keep imports from flights working. Update README with the lifecycle/cancellation contract. Use standard-library unittest and deterministic asyncio Events for concurrency tests, with no sleeps or timing assertions. Run python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v.
